Fastest in-store route

If you’re doing this one-handed with a baby, this is the shortest “grab the big wins first” route.

1

Drawing & Coloring

Grab washable markers, colored pencils, coloring paper, stickers, and dot markers first. This gets you instant-use wins.

2

Paint

Then hit washable tempera paint, brushes, palettes, foam brushes, smock/apron, and craft trays.

3

Paper & Surfaces

Grab easel paper roll, pads, canvas panels, and extra paper surfaces while you’re in the kids / paint area.

4

Wood Crafts & Glue

Finish with wooden figurines, glue sticks, safety scissors, pom-poms, stickers, and storage bins.

Shopping cards

Big photos, one-tap checkoff, and likely store area. Essentials are starred.

Easy activities to build around

Each activity below maps to items in the list above.

Paper roll paint wall

Tape out a long strip of paper and let her paint big. Extremely forgiving and toddler-friendly.

easel paperwashable tempera paintbrushessmock

Paint wooden animals / shapes

Great for painting something “real” she can keep. Easy win if you want paint that works beyond plain paper.

wood figurinestempera paintbrush set

Sticker + marker station

Very low-mess. Perfect when you want independent play for a few minutes.

washable markerssticker bookconstruction paper

Dot marker color hunt

Have her dot all the red things, blue things, circles, animals, etc. Easy and fun.

dot markerspaper pad

Collage tray

Dump pom-poms, foam shapes, scraps, and stickers on a tray with glue sticks.

glue stickspom-pomsfoam shapessafety scissors
Good parent move: if you’re overwhelmed, buy the Essentials first. That alone gives you markers, pencils, paint, brushes, paper, stickers, glue, and one special surface item.
